title: Why chunk size changes RAG quality
subtitle: Split documents without losing the context that matters
learning_objective: Explain chunking trade-offs and identify when chunk boundaries damage retrieval.

scenes.title: THE RIGHT FACT, MISSING CONTEXT
scenes.body: Your retrieval system finds a sentence with the answer—but the exception that changes its meaning was in the previous paragraph.

scenes.title: Chunks define what retrieval can see
scenes.body: Very small chunks can lose context. Very large chunks can dilute relevance and consume more context-window space. The best size depends on the documents and questions.

scenes.title: Measure, don't guess
scenes.body: Create a small set of representative questions. Compare retrieval relevance and answer quality across chunk sizes, overlap, and metadata filters.

scenes.question: What is the main risk of chunks that are too small?
options: They can lose context needed to interpret a fact
They always cost more storage than large chunks
scenes.explanation: A chunk may contain a fact without the surrounding definition, condition, or exception needed to use it correctly.

scenes.title: Remember this
scenes.body: Chunk around meaning and evaluate retrieval against realistic questions, not just chunk count.
